In [[algebraic number theory]], a '''ring class field''' is the [[abelian extension]] of an [[algebraic number field]] <math>K</math> associated by [[class field theory]] to the '''ring class group''' of some [[order (ring theory)|order]] <math>\mathcal{O}</math> of the [[ring of integers]] of <math>K</math>.{{sfnp|Frey|Lange|2006|p=[https://books.google.com/books?id=w6b0yhURTkQC&pg=PA99 99]}}

==Examples==
* Let <math>K</math> be any number field. The ring class field for the maximal order <math>\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{O}_K</math> is the [[Hilbert class field]] <math>H</math>.

* Let <math>K=\Q(\sqrt{-n})</math>. 
** The ring class field for the order <math>\mathcal{O}=\Z[\sqrt{-n}]</math> is <math>L=K(a)</math>, where <math>a</math> is an [[algebraic integer]] with [[minimal polynomial (field theory)|minimal polynomial]] over <math>\Q</math> of [[degree of a polynomial|degree]] <math>h(-4n)</math>, the [[Ideal class group|class number]] of an order with discriminant <math>-4n</math>.{{clarification needed|date=August 2026}} Moreover, if <math>p</math> is an [[parity (mathematics)|odd]] [[prime number|prime]] not dividing <math>n</math>, then <math>p</math> [[splitting of prime ideals in Galois extensions|splits completely]] in <math>L</math> if and only if <math>p</math> splits completely in <math>K</math>.

** If <math>\mathcal{O}</math> is an order and <math>a</math> is a proper [[fractional ideal|fractional ''O''-ideal]]; i.e.
:::<math>\{x\in K^\times: xa\subset a\}=\mathcal{O}</math>,
::write <math>j(a)</math> for the [[j-invariant|''j''-invariant]] of the associated [[elliptic curve]]. Then  <math>K(j(a))</math> is the ring class field of <math>\mathcal{O}</math> and <math>j(a)</math> is an algebraic integer.
